newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alenia seeks entry into Airbus work.
newsitem.headline: Alenia seeks entry into Airbus work.

text.p: Alenia SpA, the aerospace unit of Italy's Finmeccanica holding company, wants to work on Airbus Industrie derivative products as an entry into participating in building the consortium's passenger planes.
"The practical approach (is) to allow us to enter programme by programme, using new developments, the derivatives," Alenia's president and chief operating officer Giorgio Zappa said.
"I think with this step-by-step approach we will be offered the opportunity to enter the Airbus core of the family," he said.
The aim was "a global cooperation" with Airbus, he said.
The core Airbus products are the A320 narrow-body family and the A330/340 wide-body, long-haul jets. Airbus is developing the A330 and A340 series to meet competition from Boeing products.

Alenia is not a member of the Airbus consortium for civilian passenger jets but is a member of its subsidiary Airbus Military Company (AMC) set up to manage the planned Future Large Aircraft (FLA) project.
Alenia is a subcontractor for McDonnell Douglas and Boeing Co on their passenger jets.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA (CASA) of Spain.
